issues.legal_issue: A criminal court cannot take cognizance of alleged false evidence in a statutory tribunal proceeding without a written complaint from the tribunal when the law deems it a civil court for that purpose.
material_facts: The appellants were alleged to have filed false affidavits in allotment proceedings before a Rent Control Officer.
The Rent Control Officer was authorized to perform the relevant functions of the District Magistrate under the rent legislation.
The legislation deemed the District Magistrate and the relevant authorities to be civil courts for the purposes of the specified offences of giving false evidence and contempt.
The complainant, rather than the Rent Control Officer or another court, filed the complaint; no written complaint from the forum was made.
issues.conclusion: The criminal court had no jurisdiction to take cognizance of the alleged offence of giving false evidence because the required written complaint from the forum was absent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 195(1)(b)(i) and 195(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, cognizance of an offence under Section 193 of the Indian Penal Code alleged to have been committed in or in relation to a proceeding in a court requires a written complaint from that court or a court to which it is subordinate. The rent legislation, including Sections 3(c) and 34, deemed the relevant authority to be a civil court for the purposes of Section 193 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.false_evidence_prosecution: The proceeding seeks criminal cognizance for allegedly giving or fabricating false evidence.
predicates.statutory_forum_deemed_court_for_offence: The forum conducting the underlying proceeding is treated by law as a civil court for the alleged offence.
predicates.alleged_false_evidence_related_to_forum_: The alleged false evidence was given in or in relation to a proceeding before that forum.
predicates.no_written_complaint_from_forum: No written complaint was made by the forum or a court to which it is subordinate.

issues.definition: When a false-evidence prosecution concerns a proceeding before a forum treated as a court for that offence, the absence of a written complaint from the forum bars cognizance.

issues.legal_issue: A complaint does not support cognizance of causing evidence to disappear or giving false information to screen an offender when it identifies neither the evidence allegedly destroyed nor the offence or false information involved.
material_facts: The complainant invoked the offence of causing evidence to disappear or giving false information to screen an offender.
The complaint did not identify any existing evidence that the appellants had caused to disappear.
The complaint did not identify an offence whose evidence was destroyed or specify false information given to screen an offender.
issues.conclusion: The allegations did not constitute the alleged offence, and the complaint on that count was liable to be quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 201 of the Indian Penal Code requires allegations showing that evidence of an offence was caused to disappear, or that false information was given, with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment. A bare reference to the offence, without allegations addressing its essential facts, does not support cognizance. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.criminal_complaint_for_screening_offence: The proceeding is a criminal complaint alleging that evidence was concealed or false information was given to screen an offender.
predicates.no_disappeared_evidence_identified: The complaint does not identify evidence that existed and was caused to disappear.
predicates.no_screening_information_or_underlying_o: The complaint does not identify the offence involved or false information given to screen its perpetrator.

issues.definition: A screening-offence complaint is insufficient for cognizance when it identifies neither disappeared evidence nor the offence or screening information involved.

issues.legal_issue: The rejection of a statement in contested proceedings does not by itself establish that the statement was knowingly false for the purpose of a criminal charge based on a false declaration.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that statements in affidavits filed in allotment proceedings were false but did not identify a specific false statement.
The complainant did not set out the alleged falsity by reference to the truth established in a document.
An appellate authority did not accept the allottee’s assertion that he occupied a room in the premises, but the record did not establish that the assertion was knowingly false.
issues.conclusion: The rejected assertion did not, by itself, establish an offence based on a false declaration, and the complaint on this count was liable to be quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 199 of the Indian Penal Code concerns a false statement in a declaration receivable as evidence. The alleged statement must be identified and its falsity shown by reference to the truth established in a document; rejection of a party’s evidence, including on the basis of the burden of proof, does not alone establish falsity. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.false_declaration_complaint: The proceeding is a criminal complaint alleging a false statement in a declaration receivable as evidence.
predicates.statement_not_specifically_identified: The complaint does not identify the particular statement alleged to be false.
predicates.falsity_not_supported_by_documentary_tru: The complaint does not show the statement’s falsity by reference to the truth established in a document.
predicates.evidence_rejected_only_after_contested_a: The statement was not accepted after the decision-maker assessed contested evidence, without a finding that it was knowingly false.

issues.definition: A false-declaration complaint does not establish criminal falsity where the statement is unspecified, its falsity is not anchored to documentary truth, and its rejection resulted only from an assessment of contested evidence.

issues.legal_issue: The High Court may use its inherent criminal jurisdiction to quash a prosecution that is an abuse of process, including a prosecution brought by a frustrated litigant after adverse proceedings when the allegations do not substantiate the charged offences.
material_facts: The complainant had unsuccessfully challenged the allotment in the rent-control proceedings before filing the criminal complaint.
A separate civil dispute between the parties was pending.
The complaint followed the adverse allotment proceedings and alleged offences based on affidavits filed in those proceedings.
The allegations did not identify evidence destroyed for the alleged screening offence, and the rejection of a disputed statement did not establish that it was knowingly false.
issues.conclusion: The criminal complaint was an abuse of the process of law; the appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the criminal proceedings were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, permits the High Court to exercise its inherent jurisdiction to prevent abuse of the process of a criminal court. A litigant’s frustration at losing related proceedings does not justify invoking criminal jurisdiction where the complaint’s allegations do not support the charged offences. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.criminal_proceeding: The matter is a criminal proceeding initiated by a complaint.
predicates.complaint_follows_adverse_related_procee: The complainant brought the criminal complaint after an adverse result in related proceedings.
predicates.complainant_has_pending_related_dispute: A related civil or other dispute between the parties remains pending.
predicates.complainant_is_frustrated_by_adverse_res: The complaint was brought as an expression of frustration at the complainant’s adverse result in related proceedings.
predicates.charged_offences_lack_supporting_allegat: The complaint does not allege facts sufficient to support the offences charged.

issues.definition: A criminal proceeding is an abuse of process warranting quashing when it follows adverse related proceedings and the charged offences lack supporting allegations, particularly where a related dispute remains pending or the complaint reflects frustration with the adverse result.
